@graph.name: Gluten-Free Cornbread
@graph.description: This cornbread recipe is gluten-free thanks to almond flour! It's absolutely delicious with light sweetness, crisp edges and bold corn flavor. Recipe yields up to 16 modest slices.
recipeIngredient: 1 ½ cups (300 grams) cornmeal, medium-grind or finer*
1 ½ cups milk of choice***, at room temperature
Optional serving suggestions: additional butter, honey or jam

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit. In a large bowl, combine the cornmeal, almond flour, salt, baking powder and baking soda. Stir to combine, and set aside. In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs and maple syrup until fully blended. Add the milk and whisk until evenly combined.
Pour the liquid into the dry mixture, and stir just until moistened through (we’ll stir it more soon). Set it aside while you melt the butter (this resting time gives the cornmeal time to soften).

Meanwhile, place the butter in a large (12-inch) cast iron skillet. Put the skillet in the oven to melt the butter, about 5 to 13 minutes (keep an extra eye on it as time goes on—we want it to get bubbly and lightly browned, but not burnt).
When the butter is melted and golden, use oven mitts (the skillet is crazy hot!) to remove the skillet from the oven, and give it a gentle swirl to lightly coat about an inch up the sides.
Pour the melted butter into the batter and stir just until incorporated. Pour the batter back into the hot skillet, using a spatula to scrape all of the batter from the bowl into the skillet.

Carefully return the skillet to the oven and bake until the bread is brown around the edge, springy to the touch, and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean with just a few crumbs, 25 to 30 minutes. Carefully (with oven mitts), place the skillet on a cooling rack. Let it cool for at least 5 minutes before slicing and serving—perhaps with extra butter, honey or jam on the side.
This cornbread will keep at room temperature in a sealed container for up to 3 days, or up to a week in the refrigerator. You can also freeze it for up to 3 months. Gently reheat before serving.

review.reviewBody: I already make a wonderful cornbread, so this is something amazing to lower that carb count.  One question though, Kate:  I also try to lighten recipes and make them lower in saturated fat.  Can skim milk be used with this?  Also, can I just use egg whites?  Many thanks...you rock!

Fantastic gluten free cornbread! I added two chopped jalapeños as described in  optional add-ins section. Reduced the maple syrup to 2 tablespoons because I didn’t want sweet cornbread with the jalapeños. Used home made cashew milk. I’ve tried many gluten free cornbread recipes and this one is the best! Especially love baking it in a cast iron skillet.

I made this with a blue corn meal and honey as the sweetener. It is a super easy recipe that is very flavorful. It baked perfectly and released easily from the pan. I would absolutely make this again.
